rv.q: The Honey Trap comes together with devastating force in its final moments.
McGann constructs his story like a taut-as-a-violin-string thriller, slowly building the tension and revising history as different narrators tell their versions of the same events.
The Honey Trap is one of the most riveting psychological thrillers I've seen onstage in some time.
This is one of the strongest new plays Irish Rep has offered in a good long while.
'The Honey Trap' has much to say to us, living in a world wracked by a never-ending search for vengeance; the modern resonances are almost too obvious to mention.
Irish Rep's premiere delivers an undeniably entertaining two hours.

Though The Honey Trap clamps down in an emotionally stunning conclusion, a reviewer's mild query is whether in the Dave/Charlie twist does McGann risk confusing literally inclined spectators too much before revealing his devastating destination?
But this play picks a narrower path and we end up watching Dave stage his own personal skin-crawling honey trap which frustratingly did not illuminate much beyond his rage.

The Honey Trap's biggest success is the way it doesn't brow beat the higher level intellectual concepts onto the viewer, but rather presents a very frequent situation in a very extreme context to ask some questions about the little white lies that sweeten our recounting of how something happened.
Both an excellent cast and stellar direction makes this craftily written play riveting.
Leo McGann's 'The Honey Trap,' now at Irish Repertory Theatre in a taut, unnerving production, understands that trauma doesn't fade with time; it just finds new ways to destroy you.
The Honey Trap is another prize, another winner, on Irish Repertory Theatre's shelf of good historical dramas with deep psychological underpinnings that make for a great night out at the theatre.
McGann ramps up the tension to an ending that is both shockingly unexpected and yet feels absolutely right.
With a strong ensemble and a script that refuses easy answers, this production offers audiences both a gripping story and a sobering reminder of how the past continues to shadow the present.
Leo McGann's The Honey Trap is a gripping thriller that explores the Troubles in a unique and compelling way.
